STANCE: for
STATEMENT: I used Lintwise for six months on my previous team. It caught real bugs—null dereferences, off-by-one errors—that would have shipped to production otherwise. That alone justifies it. My one concern: it added roughly 4 minutes to our CI pipeline. Our builds already average 11 minutes, so we're looking at 15 minutes per merge. Across twenty people pushing multiple PRs a day, that's real friction. I'd vote for the motion, but I'd ask: can we run Lintwise as a fast pre-check *before* the full build kicks off, so we fail early and don't burn the full 11 minutes on a lint failure? If we can scope it to changed files only, the overhead shrinks a lot. I support adoption with that optimization as a follow-up ticket.
TLDR: none

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: Priya's pre-check idea is exactly right, and I'll own the implementation. Here's my concern though: with twenty devs pushing multiple PRs daily, even a four-minute lint stage sits in the queue ahead of the build. If Lintwise runs *inside* the 11-minute job, every lint failure still occupies a CI runner slot for its duration. I need it as a separate, parallel gate—fail in under 90 seconds, never touch the build queue. I also need Lintwise scoped to changed files only; a full-repo scan on a monorepo will not finish in ninety seconds. I'll prototype the two-stage pipeline this sprint. Condition for my "for": Lintwise must not increase average queue wait beyond 90 seconds, and it must run outside the build job entirely.
TLDR: none

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: I support adoption. A mandatory pre-merge gate is exactly where secrets and vulnerable dependencies should be caught—before they reach main. However, my support is conditional on two things. First, I need confirmation that Lintwise's rule set actually covers hardcoded secrets, tokens, and known-vulnerable dependency versions, not just style and null-safety. If it doesn't, we're adding a gate that gives false security confidence. Second, Marcus's 90-second budget worries me. A meaningful dependency-manifest scan across a monorepo can exceed that. I'd accept the 90-second lint gate for code-quality rules, but I want a separate, non-blocking security scan (secrets + dependency CVE check) that runs in parallel and reports within the same PR, even if it takes longer. Priya's changed-files-only optimization is fine for lint rules; I'd want the security scan to cover the full lockfile regardless of which files changed. I'll vote for with those two follow-up tickets filed before rollout.
TLDR: For the motion, but require (1) confirmation Lintwise covers secrets and vulnerable dependencies, not just code-quality rules, and (2) a separate parallel security scan (full lockfile, secrets check) that isn't squeezed into Marcus's 90-second budget. File both as tickets before rollout.

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: I tried Lintwise on a small side project—maybe three thousand lines of JavaScript. It flagged a few unused variables and one potential null access. Useful, sure, but honestly the signal-to-noise on a toy repo isn't the same as a monorepo with twenty devs. I'm for adoption, but I want the JavaScript rule set tuned before we make it blocking. On my side project I disabled six rules that were pure style noise; I don't want to file six tickets per PR just to silence formatting warnings. Marcus's ninety-second gate and Priya's changed-files scoping both address my speed concern. One practical ask: let us run Lintwise locally with the same config before pushing, so I'm not waiting ninety seconds in CI to learn I left a console.log in. I'll support this once the JS ruleset is curated and a local pre-commit hook ships.
TLDR: For adoption, but the JavaScript ruleset needs curation before it's blocking—my side-project experience showed too many style-noise rules. Support Marcus's 90s parallel gate and changed-files scoping. Require a local pre-commit hook with the same config so devs catch issues before CI.

STANCE: undecided
STATEMENT: I haven't used Lintwise, so I'm cautious about making it blocking before I know what it catches in Python and SQL. My pipelines are mostly SQL embedded in Python—bad joins, missing WHERE clauses on partitioned tables, schema drift. Does Lintwise lint SQL, or treat .sql files as opaque strings? If Python-only, it misses my highest-risk surface. I'm not against adoption, but I want a one-week advisory trial on my pipeline repos with results visible to me before it gates merges. I also need confirmation that Marcus's ninety-second budget holds when Lintwise parses thousands of lines of SQL, not just Python. If SQL coverage is thin, I'd prefer it advisory on my repos until we validate it.
TLDR: No hands-on experience with Lintwise; unsure it covers SQL—the riskiest part of my pipelines. Want a one-week advisory trial on my repos and proof the 90-second budget survives SQL parsing before it blocks merges.

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: I've read Lintwise's docs. Its rule catalog is strong on null-safety, resource leaks, and off-by-one patterns—exactly the classes that leak into production and waste QA cycles. That's real signal. My concern is noise. The default rule set ships roughly forty style rules that don't affect correctness. If those gate merges, devs ignore the gate entirely and we lose real signal. I support adoption with one hard condition: ship a curated blocking ruleset—correctness and safety only—and demote style rules to advisory. QA will own false-positive triage for the first two sprints. I back Marcus's parallel 90-second gate and Tom's pre-commit hook; catching issues locally preserves CI capacity and keeps failure reasons unambiguous for QA triage.
TLDR: For adoption. Require a curated blocking ruleset (correctness and safety only; style demoted to advisory) so the gate stays high-signal. QA owns false-positive triage for two sprints. Supports Marcus's parallel 90-second gate and Tom's pre-commit hook to preserve CI capacity and keep failure reasons clear.

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: I'm for adoption. As merge-policy owner, I need one uniform rule for twenty devs on a monorepo—Lintwise as a blocking gate is the right consistency lever. But I won't sign off on a gate that makes devs wait. Marcus's parallel 90-second pre-check, running outside the build queue, is the architecture I'll approve. Sana's advisory trial is reasonable—two weeks on SQL-heavy repos, then we flip to blocking. Lars's curation is non-negotiable: blocking covers correctness and safety only; style stays advisory. Tom's pre-commit hook ships day one so CI failures are rare, not routine. I'll write the merge-policy update this sprint: Lintwise blocks merge on blocking-rule violations; advisory findings appear as PR comments, not gates. Elena's security scan gets its own ticket and timeline—Marcus's 90-second budget stays untouched.
TLDR: For adoption with a parallel 90-second gate outside the build queue, a curated correctness-only blocking ruleset (style is advisory), a two-week advisory trial for SQL repos, a day-one pre-commit hook, and a separate security-scan ticket. I own the merge-policy rewrite this sprint.

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: I'm for this. As someone newer here, I often second-guess whether my code matches team expectations—spacing, naming, error handling. An automated checker removes that guesswork and gives me a clear signal before I open a PR. Tom's pre-commit hook matters most to me: catching a violation locally in seconds beats seeing a red X on CI after eleven minutes. I agree blocking rules should cover only correctness and safety—style noise would just confuse me more. One ask: a short "what Lintwise flags and why" guide for new devs, so I learn conventions instead of Googling rule IDs.
TLDR: For adoption. Pre-commit hook and correctness/safety-only blocking rules matter most to me; a brief rule-explanation guide for newcomers would help me learn conventions faster.

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: I ran Lintwise for six months on my old backend team. It caught real defects—race conditions in our queue workers, a null-deref that would have taken down a payment path. That's why I'm for. But those four minutes were painful when our builds were already tight. I back Marcus's parallel 90-second gate and changed-files scoping; a full monorepo lint on twenty devs' daily PRs will not fit that budget. I also want Sana's SQL advisory trial—Lintwise's SQL rules on my old team were noisy and missed real query-plan issues. Block on correctness and safety only; style stays advisory. I'll help Marcus prototype the gate this sprint.
TLDR: Six months of hands-on use showed Lintwise catches real backend bugs, but four extra CI minutes are painful. Support adoption conditional on Marcus's parallel 90-second gate, changed-files-only scoping, Sana's SQL advisory trial, and a correctness/safety-only blocking ruleset. Will help prototype.

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: As the person who owns this pipeline, I'll say plainly: a 4-minute lint stage *inside* the 11-minute build is unacceptable. That's 15 minutes per runner slot, and with twenty devs pushing multiple PRs daily, my queue balloons and people start gaming the system—merging during off-peak windows, stacking retries. Marcus's parallel 90-second gate is the architecture I need, and I'll provide the runner configuration. But two conditions from my side: the lint gate must run on a *dedicated* runner pool, not share slots with build jobs, or a PR spike starves builds just the same. And changed-files scoping is non-negotiable—full monorepo lint will blow the 90-second budget on any PR touching shared utilities. Tom's pre-commit hook is my favorite part: every issue caught locally is a pipeline that never enters my queue. I'll set up the runner pool and alerting thresholds this sprint.
TLDR: None

STANCE: for
STATEMENT: I support adoption, but I need to be blunt about scope. Lintwise is a code-quality checker. It is not a secrets scanner and it is not a dependency-vulnerability scanner. If we merge it as "the gate," people will assume security is covered. It isn't. My requirement: a separate, parallel security stage—git-secrets or equivalent for credential leaks in diffs, plus a lockfile audit for known CVEs—that runs alongside Marcus's 90-second lint gate but is *not* merged into it. Security findings must block independently and report through a channel I own, so a leaked API key doesn't get buried under a style warning. I also need the advisory-trial repos to include one with historical secret leaks so I can validate detection coverage before rollout. I'll write the security-scan ticket this sprint.
TLDR: For adoption, but Lintwise must not be conflated with security scanning. Require a separate parallel stage for secrets detection and dependency CVE auditing, blocking independently with its own reporting channel. Include a known-secret-leak repo in the advisory trial to validate coverage before it blocks merges. Security-scan ticket filed this sprint.
